issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem a1 claims that combining Proposition a14 with Lemma a20 yields a pseudospectral area contribution with coefficient 2n^2\log(R/\eta_0) times f/\eta^2. But Proposition a14 contributes a factor [3n\lg(3R/\eta_0)+3\lg(2\eta_0/\tau_0)]\cdot n^2/\eta_2^2 (from 1/(\tau_0\eps^2) = n^2/\eta_0^2) and Lemma a20 contributes \pi R^2. The correct coefficient is of order n^3R^2\log(R/\eta), exceeding 2n^2\log(R/\eta_0) by a factor of order nR^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2n^2\log(R/\eta_0) with the correct coefficient derived from Proposition a14 and Lemma a20 and re-verify that the subsequent application of Proposition a19 yields O(n^{-K}).
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate tail bound on \kappa_V in the proof of Theorem a1 is too optimistic by a factor of order nR^2. The final Theorem a1 bounds are weaker and survive correction.
issues.title: Wrong coefficient for pseudospectral area term in Theorem a1 proof
issues.why_classification: A local fix to one coefficient in one display. The corrected bound still yields O(n^{-K}) tail probabilities so all substantive claims survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Take it to be that upper bound divided by $R^{2K+2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof sets \eta^{2/3} = \rho^{1+K}/(8n^{4+K}R^{4K+2}) (the upper bound from Proposition a19 divided by R^{2K+2}) and defines \tau = 1/(n^2\eta^{2/3}). This gives \tau = 8n^{2+K}R^{4K+2}/\rho^{1+K}, not 8n^{3+2K}R^{2K} as displayed. The ratio of the displayed threshold to \tau is (n\rho)^{1+K}/R^{2K+2} which is less than 1 whenever R > n\rho, so the displayed threshold is smaller than \tau and the claimed bound does not follow from the preceding inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the threshold to 8n^{2+K}R^{4K+2}/\rho^{1+K} and re-verify the subsequent bound from Proposition a19 at that threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The specific tail threshold in the proof of Theorem a1 is not established. The final theorem bounds (exponents 10K and 35K) are weaker than what the corrected threshold yields and remain valid.
issues.title: Incorrect threshold for kappa squared tail bound in Theorem a1 proof
issues.why_classification: A single-formula correction to one threshold. The corrected threshold yields bounds that are stronger than the theorem claims so all guarantees survive.

issues.failure_explanation: The error terms e^{-\rho n} and Pr(||M'+N||_infty >= R) from Proposition a19 are divided by \eta^2 and multiplied by R^5 (and R^2). Since \eta^2 = (\rho^{1+K}/(8n^{4++K}R^{4K+2}))^3, the factor R^5/\eta^2 = 512 R^{11+12K} n^{12+3K}/\rho^{3+3K} can greatly exceed R^{20K}. The bound R^{20K}e^{-\rho n} is therefore not a valid upper bound for these terms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace R^{20K}e^{-\rho n} with the correct bound R^5 e^{-\rho n}/\eta^2 + R^2 e^{-\rho n}/\eta^2 and verify it is O(n^{-K}).
issues.overall_effect: The error bound in the proof of Theorem a1 is wrong. The corrected error term R^5 e^{-\rho n}/\eta^2 is still O(n^{-K}) under the theorem's hypotheses so the conclusion survives.
issues.title: Incorrect error term bound in Theorem a1 proof
issues.why_classification: A local correction to one error bound in one display. The corrected bound is still O(n^{-K}) so the final guarantee is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The inductive step produces an extra factor sqrt(1-1/|J|) < 1 at each stage, so the claimed inductive hypothesis d_J >= \eta^{|J|-1}/(2^{|J|} sqrt(n)) is not established. The product of these factors over |J| = 2,...,n equals prod sqrt(1-1/j) = 1/sqrt(n), not 1/n as used. The proof therefore establishes d_{[n]} >= \eta^{n-1}/(2^n n) and \kappa_V(A) <= n^{3/2} 2^n \eta^{1-n}, not the stated n 2^n \eta^{1-n}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change n to n^{3/2} in the statement of Proposition a11.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition a11's bound is stronger than what the proof establishes by a factor of sqrt(n). The qualitative exponential bound on \kappa_V in terms of 1/\eta is preserved and all downstream uses survive with the weaker bound.
issues.title: Exponential kappa_V bound off by sqrt(n) factor in Proposition a11
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol change to the statement preserves every substantive claim and guarantee. The corrected bound has the same form and all downstream results are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma a11 gives \kappa_V(A) <= n 2^n (R/\eta_0)^{n-1} after normalization so \kappa_V^2 <= n^2 4^n (R/\eta_0)^{2n-2}. The bootstrap threshold satisfies \tau_K >= \eta_0(3R/\eta_0)^n which grows like (R/\eta_0)^n. But \kappa_V^2 grows like (R/\eta_0)^{2n}. The ratio \kappa_V^2/\tau_K ~ n^2(4/3)^n(R/\eta_0)^{n-2}/\eta_0 diverges for R > \eta_0 so the claimed implication F(\tau_K) fails.

failure_location.quote: Lemma \ref{a11} combined with (\ref{a27}) implies $G\wedge\magn{A}\le R\implies F(\tau_K)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Increase K from ceil(n lg(3R/\eta_0) + lg(\eta_0/\tau_0)) to approximately ceil(2n lg(3R/\eta_0) + 2n + lg(\eta_0/\tau_0)) so that \tau_K exceeds \kappa_V^2, and adjust the coefficient in the bound accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The bootstrap in Proposition a14 does not terminate at step K as claimed. The coefficient of the pseudospectral area term in Proposition a14's bound is unreliable. Theorem a1's combined bound which uses Proposition a14 is affected.
issues.title: Bootstrap termination claim is false in Proposition a14
issues.why_classification: The fix is a parameter adjustment (doubling K) that preserves the form of the bound and all downstream results. No new argument or construction is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The integral over {|z| <= R+\eps} has area \pi(R+\eps)^2 not \pi R^2. The proof writes an equality with \pi R^2 \sup but the correct bound is \pi(R+\eps)^2 \sup. The difference \pi(2R\eps + \eps^2) is not absorbed by the e^{-\Omega(R)} error term for polynomially small \eps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \pi R^2 with \pi(R+\eps)^2 in the statement and proof of Lemma a20.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma a20's stated bound is too tight by a factor (1+\eps/R)^2. The pseudospectral area estimate used in Theorem a1's proof inherits this error.
issues.title: Wrong area factor in pseudospectral area bound of Lemma a20
issues.why_classification: A constant-factor correction in one lemma's statement. All downstream uses work with (R+\eps)^2 <= 2R^2 so every substantive claim and guarantee survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\net$ be an $r$-net of the disk of radius $R$.

issues.failure_explanation: With an r-net and |\lambda_i - \lambda_j| <= r, the nearest net point z to the midpoint satisfies |z - \lambda_i| <= 3r/2 and |z - \lambda_j| <= 3r/2, not both <= r. Even the weaker product bound |\lambda_i-z||\lambda_j-z| <= r^2 can fail: at the nearest net point the product reaches up to 5r^2/4. A finer net (e.g. r/2-net) or a larger constant in the product bound is needed.

failure_location.quote: if they're both inside the disk, then there must be some $z\in\net$ such that $\lambda_i,\lambda_j\in\ball(z,r)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an r/2-net (changing the prefactor to 4\pi R^2/r^2) or replace r^2 by 5r^2/4 in the product bound and adjust the subsequent case split accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The net argument in Lemma a21's proof is incorrect so the lemma's prefactor \pi R^2/r^2 and subsequent bounds on Pr(\eta <= r) are unreliable as stated. Theorem a1's gap bound which uses Lemma a21 is affected.
issues.title: Net argument with r-net fails in Lemma a21
issues.why_classification: A constant-factor adjustment to one lemma's proof and statement. All downstream results work with the corrected constant so every substantive claim and guarantee survives.
